title: Re-rate when the swings are redrawn

blocks.text: A city bus operator values its projects by rider-hours saved, accidents avoided and savings ($k). Its board set swing ratings once (the biggest swing rated 100, the others as a share of it) against references `old_reference`. Next year the planners redraw the swings: `new_reference` gives each measure's new swing, in the same units. The board did not change its mind about what an accident or a rider-hour is worth, only about how big the swings are.

Write `rerate(ratings, old_reference, new_reference)` in `swings.py`, returning ratings for the new swings that keep the price of every measure in every other (`price`, given, computes one), and that follow the convention again: the biggest swing is rated 100 and the others as a share of it.
Before coding, write down what a price is in terms of a rating, its reference and the ratings' total, and ask which part may change. About three lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from swings import price, rerate

old = {"delay": 500, "injuries": 4, "savings": 800}
ratings = {"delay": 100, "injuries": 70, "savings": 30}

new = rerate(ratings, old, {**old, "injuries": 2})
print("injuries swing 4 -> 2:", {m: round(r, 3) for m, r in new.items()})
other = {"delay": 1_000, "injuries": 4, "savings": 400}
again = rerate(ratings, old, other)
print("delay 1000, savings 400:", {m: round(r, 3) for m, r in again.items()})
print("delay in savings, old ratings:", round(price(ratings, old, "delay", "savings"), 4))
print("delay in savings, rerated:", round(price(again, other, "delay", "savings"), 4))

cases.says: a swing that doubles or halves gets a rating that doubles or halves, worked out by hand
every measure's price in the base measure is the same before and after
the projects keep their order under the new references and ratings, which the old ratings would not
when another measure's swing becomes the biggest, the ratings are restated so that it is 100
